subject: Skybridge: Data export safeguards, DPF evidence & DPA annex — asks and next steps
messages:
From: Elaine Morris <elaine.morris@skybridgehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, procurement@skybridgehealth.com
Cc: Skybridge Legal <legal@skybridgehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: Cross-border transfer safeguards + DPF evidence (Skybridge RFP)

Hi Ben —

Thanks for taking our call last week. Skybridge is running a brief vendor assessment for cross-border data transfers and needs the following to progress procurement:

1) Example DPA annex (transfer clauses / SCCs / DPF mapping)
2) Technical and organizational safeguards evidence for EU->US exports (logs, retention, encryption, subprocessors, key custody details)
3) A short playbook on how Redwood handles temporary caching/prefix storage and KV exports when customers use our hosted API
4) Any SOC2 / ISO references and a high-level list of subprocessors with locations

We attached our standard RFI excel (procurement timeline in tab 1). Can we get an initial package by end of week? Procurement would like to circulate to security and legal.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a 30m call if that helps.

Elaine Morris
Sr. Procurement Manager, Skybridge Health
procurement@skybridgehealth.com

Ben / Karthik —

Thanks Ben. Quick notes for the DPA annex draft I'm preparing:

- We will include DPF mapping for EU->US transfers using EU SCCs as baseline and reference our published Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) wording.
- For subprocessors we will provide a redacted list with country locations; full list available in the appendix under NDA if they require vendor-by-vendor legal review.
- Retention: default logs retention 90 days (configurable), with options for longer retention on Dedicated/Private deployments — will call this out.
- Key custody: KMS support for BYOK on Private deployments, Redwood-managed KMS for hosted (we provide key rotation schedule).

I will attach a first-pass annex and highlight clauses I think Skybridge often asks to redline (data categories, export mechanisms, audit rights). Monica, please attach the technical control matrix for Skybridge's security team.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 11:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: Cross-border transfer safeguards + DPF evidence (Skybridge RFP)

Elaine / team —

Attaching the technical evidence pack and an export controls matrix. Short answers below for procurement/security reviewers:

- Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit; AES-256 at rest for hosted. Customer-managed keys available in Redwood Private (BYOK) and Dedicated (KMS integration).
- KV cache / prefix handling: ephemeral caches retained for up to 60s in runtime; persisted traces stored only when logging enabled by customer. We detail per-endpoint caching policies in the playbook.
- Logs & audit: request traces and token-level metrics retained by default for 90 days; longer retention available under contract for Dedicated/Private.
- Access controls: role-based admin controls, token scoping, and session MFA for console access.
- Subprocessors: primary compute partners in us-west-2 and eu-west-1; storage backups in us-central. Full CSV attached.
- Evidence: SOC2 Type II summary link included in the pack; we can provide cert copy under NDA.

Monica Patel
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Attachments: export_controls_matrix.csv; technical_evidence_pack.zip
Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bC_example_drive_link

Subject: Re: Request: Cross-border transfer safeguards + DPF evidence (Skybridge RFP)

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the attachments — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from legal/security after a quick read: 

1) Transfer mechanism: we need clear language on fallback when SCCs are applied versus when the DPF supplemental measures are referenced. Can you give two short example clauses (one SCC-forward, one DPF-forward) we can copy into our template?
2) Processor role: confirm Redwood operates as a processor in the context of our API use, and whether any subprocessor sometimes acts as a processor for logging services (we want explicit callouts).
3) KV caching: can you confirm the maximum timeframe for persisted cache in hosted mode and whether it contains raw input prompts or only tokenized vectors?

Procurement also asked for the DPA annex as an editable file (so we can redline). If you can send the annex + example clauses and a single consolidated ZIP by EOD CET, that would keep our timeline intact for legal review.

Elaine Morris
Sr. Procurement Manager, Skybridge Health

Subject: Re: Request: Cross-border transfer safeguards + DPF evidence (Skybridge RFP)

Elaine —

Appreciate the clarifying questions. Summary & next steps below; consolidated ZIP attached in this thread for procurement/legal.

Quick answers:
- Processor role: Redwood will be Processor for API/hosting. Some subprocessors (e.g., logging/observability partner) will have limited processing responsibilities acting under Redwood as a subprocessor; we call these out in the CSV.
- KV caching: hosted runtime uses ephemeral KV caches; persisted cache for diagnostics/logging occurs only when customer enables logging and is limited to the minimum token metadata required. Max persisted retention in hosted mode is 90 days by default; Dedicated/Private options available for custom retention. Caches do not store raw PII beyond what is included in customer payloads — we highlight tokenization handling in the playbook.
- Transfer mechanism examples: included two short example clauses in the annex (SCC-forward and DPF-forward) — see pages 3-4 of dpa_annex_template_v2.docx.

Deliverables attached: redwood_crossborder_playbook.pdf; dpa_annex_template_v2.docx; export_controls_matrix.csv; technical_evidence_pack.zip. I also added a short mutual action plan below to keep the procurement timeline on track.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
- 22 Nov (today): Redwood sends consolidated evidence package and editable annex (done).
- 24 Nov: Skybridge security/legal initial redlines returned.
- 28 Nov: Redwood receives redlines and provides final comments / approved DPA draft.
- 01 Dec: DocuSign DPA prepared and shared with Skybridge contract owner (HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-9021).

If that timeline works, we'll prepare the DocuSign link and a short 30m walk-through for legal/security next week.
